newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares at precarious two year high - brokers.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares at precarious two year high - brokers.

text.p: Egyptian shares leaped to their highest level in over two years on Tuesday but brokers described the move as sudden and said it left the bourse unsteady.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) overall index rose 1.2 percent to 239.03 points, its highest level since December 1994.
Volume was a large 132.2 million pounds ($38.9 million) but most of that came from the listing of shares worth 115 million in newly privatised General Storage and Silos.
"There's absolutely no reason for the market to rise by this much while trading is quite slow," said broker Youssef Khalil of Delta EAB. "Even the mills are not doing as well as before."
Brokers said slight gains in the market-leading milling sector had contributed to the overall rise but trade was thin.
Central and West Delta Flour Mills rose 0.50 pounds to 59.00 and Southern Cairo Flour Mills gained 1.50 to 51.50 pounds.

The day's biggest gainer was Arab Cotton Ginning which soared 17.7 percent to 41.51 pounds. Brokers said some investors were scooping up as many shares as they can to get into the newly-privatised company's board.
But the blue chip realty sector dragged the bourse lower.
Profit-taking hit Medinet Nasr Housing and Development, which buoyed the bourse last week, and the shares slipped 1.81 percent to 184.00 pounds.

Rumours that the state had changed its mind about privatising Heliopolis Housing pushed share prices 6.00 lower to 174.00 pounds. The government had said it might offer 40 percent of the firm but brokers said it was now thinking of selling only five percent.
The CMA index for openly traded firms rose to 358.79 points from 345.53 on Monday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose 0.06 points to 168.29 points.
